name: Example: Finding the Radius of Curvature Using the Cross Product Formula
problem: Find the radius of the osculating circle at the point where $t=0$ for the curve $\mathbf r(t)=\left\langle e^{ t}, \: e^{- t} \right\rangle.$
worked_solution:
Since we are given only the curve $\mathbf r(t),$ we will use the cross product formula to find the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t) = \dfrac{1}{\kappa(t)} = \dfrac{\|\mathbf r'(t)\|^3}{\left\|\mathbf r'(t) \times \mathbf r''(t) \right\|}
$$

First, we calculate $\mathbf r'(t),$ $\mathbf r'(0),$ and $\|\mathbf r'(0)\|\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t})⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t},\,-{e}^{-t}⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =⟨{e}^{0},\,-{e}^{-0}⟩ \\  & =⟨1,-1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(0)‖ & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate $\mathbf r''(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{-t})⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t},\,-(-{e}^{-t})⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t},\,{e}^{-t}⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(0) & =⟨{e}^{0},\,{e}^{-0}⟩ \\  & =⟨1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the cross product by considering $\mathbf r'(0)$ and $\mathbf r''(0)$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(0)\times {r}^{″}(0) & =⟨1,\,-1,\,0⟩\times ⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & \,-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}1 & \,-1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =2\,k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(0)\times {r}^{″}(0)‖ & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of curvature at $t=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(0) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(0){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(0)\times {r}^{″}(0)‖}=\frac{{(\sqrt{2})}^{3}}{\,2\,}=\sqrt{2}\,.\end{aligned}
$$
